## Summary
- Allow the `review` route on issue and pull request targets.
- Make `agent-review.yml` target-aware, preserving PR diff review while adding focused default-branch issue review.
- Thread `request_text` and trigger comment metadata into review/synthesis prompts, post issue review results back to the issue, and skip PR-only rubrics/head/orchestration behavior for issue targets.
- Update docs and tests for issue-scoped review behavior.

## Verification

- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/triage.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`
- `npm --prefix .agent run check:workflow`
- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/docs-validation.test.js`
- `git diff --check`

Closes #442

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 2ca60e5f43454e5a95a6966a8824df900298bccf -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #444 expands the `review` route so it can run on both pull requests and issues. The goal from #442/#396 is to keep PR review as diff-based review, while issue review becomes a focused default-branch review scoped by the triggering request text. The PR updates routing, review workflow inputs, prompts, posting behavior, docs, and tests to thread issue targets and request metadata through the existing review path. The implementation mostly follows existing patterns and preserves the PR-only rubrics/head/orchestration behavior where appropriate.

## Review
The implementation is close, but two unresolved warnings should be fixed before merge. One reviewer considered the PR shippable with INFO-only notes, while Codex and rubrics review both identified target validation as a real follow-up; synthesis agrees the warnings are concrete and current.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Issue synthesis prompt can still comment directly on issues | WARNING | The issue-target synthesis instructions block PR inline APIs, but they do not explicitly forbid direct issue/top-level comments even though synthesis has `issues: write` and `approve-all`. That can bypass the deterministic `post-comment.js` publisher and create duplicate or out-of-band issue comments. |
| Review workflow lacks early target preflight | WARNING | `pr_number`, `target_number`, and `target_kind` are now optional/free-form in `agent-review.yml`, but the workflow does not normalize or reject invalid targets before provider/runtime setup. Generic envelope validation later mitigates this, but direct workflow calls can still fail late or run the review prompt with unsupported target kinds. |

## Progress
- The PR implements the core requested behavior: issue `/review` is allowed, receives `request_text` and trigger metadata, and posts issue-mode synthesis back to the issue.
- Reviewer artifacts report build, focused tests, workflow checks, docs validation, and diff whitespace checks passed on head `2ca60e5f43454e5a95a6966a8824df900298bccf`.
- No existing inline comments or review threads were present before synthesis.
- Posted two new inline comments: one on `.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md` and one on `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml`.
- No comments were minimized, no replies were added, and no threads were resolved.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Issue synthesis prompt can still comment directly on issues</summary>

**Cause:** The issue branch in [`review-synthesize.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/2ca60e5f43454e5a95a6966a8824df900298bccf/.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md#L19-L30) says not to use PR inline-comment APIs, but does not say “do not post issue/top-level comments directly.” The workflow’s [`Post review comment`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/2ca60e5f43454e5a95a6966a8824df900298bccf/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L426-L440) step is meant to be the single publisher.

**Candidate solutions:** Add an explicit issue-target instruction that synthesis must return markdown only and must not call `gh` to post issue comments or top-level comments. Add a prompt test if the project wants to lock that guardrail in.

**Comments:** Inline feedback was posted at `review-synthesize.md` line 24.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Review workflow lacks early target preflight</summary>

**Cause:** The workflow now accepts optional `pr_number`, `target_kind`, and `target_number` inputs in [`agent-review.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/2ca60e5f43454e5a95a6966a8824df900298bccf/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L6-L17), then forwards fallback expressions into reviewer and synthesis runs. `run-agent-task` has generic envelope validation, but that happens after auth/runtime setup and allows target kinds outside the review prompt’s issue/PR branches.

**Candidate solutions:** Add an early normalization/preflight step or job that outputs a canonical `target_kind` and `target_number`, only allows `issue` or `pull_request`, requires a positive `target_number || pr_number`, and fails fast on conflicting inputs. Update the workflow assertions in `envelope.test.ts` to cover invalid direct/manual calls.

**Comments:** Router-dispatched review calls are already constrained to issue/PR targets, so this is not a blocking trust-boundary issue. Inline feedback was posted at `agent-review.yml` line 14.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The remaining work is concrete, low-risk branch cleanup suitable for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items
- [ ] Add an explicit issue-target synthesis prompt guardrail forbidding direct issue/top-level comments and keeping `post-comment.js` as the sole publisher.
- [ ] Add early `agent-review.yml` target validation/normalization, with tests, for supported target kind and required target number.

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #444 allows the `review` route to run on issues as well as pull requests.
- The linked issue context from #442/#396 asks for issue reviews to be focused default-branch reviews, scoped by the triggering user message, not broad audits of `main`.
- The PR updates route policy, router handoff metadata, review workflow target handling, prompts, docs, and regression tests.
- PR review behavior remains diff-based, while issue review skips PR-only head capture, inline review mechanics, rubrics review, and follow-up orchestration.

## Review
The current head addresses the prior synthesis action items: issue synthesis now returns markdown only, and `agent-review.yml` has early target validation. Reviewers mostly agree this is shippable; the remaining disagreement is whether one least-privilege workflow cleanup should block automation.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Preflight job inherits workflow write permissions | WARNING | The new `preflight` job has no checkout or API calls, but it lacks a job-level `permissions:` block and therefore inherits workflow-level write scopes. Add `permissions: {}` to keep it least-privilege. |
| Architecture overview still says review is PR-only | INFO | `.agent/docs/architecture/overall-design.md` still labels review as “PR only,” which is stale after this PR. This is documentation polish, not required branch-change work. |

## Progress
- Prior inline findings for issue synthesis direct-comment prevention and early target preflight are fixed in current head `a52aa03dd82b5c68d0d32999c0ce8f8f99590983`.
- Resolved two older same-agent inline threads: `.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md` line 24 and `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml` line 14.
- Posted one new inline comment on `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml` line 125 for the preflight permissions warning.
- No replies were added and no comments were minimized.
- Rubrics review now passes with no rubric-specific follow-up.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Preflight job inherits workflow write permissions</summary>

**Cause:** [`agent-review.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/a52aa03dd82b5c68d0d32999c0ce8f8f99590983/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L125) adds a `preflight` job under a workflow with write scopes, but the job does not override permissions. GitHub Actions jobs inherit workflow-level permissions unless scoped per job.

**Candidate solutions:** Add `permissions: {}` to the `preflight` job. If YAML style prefers expanded blocks, use an empty permissions mapping equivalent.

**Comments:** This is low-risk because the script is static and uses quoted env vars, but it is a concrete least-privilege regression from the workflow’s per-job permissions model.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Architecture overview still says review is PR-only</summary>

**Cause:** [`overall-design.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/a52aa03dd82b5c68d0d32999c0ce8f8f99590983/.agent/docs/architecture/overall-design.md#L65) still says `review (PR only, not on edit)` in the route diagram.

**Candidate solutions:** Update the diagram label to reflect PR and issue review targets.

**Comments:** This is optional documentation cleanup; the main usage docs and runtime behavior are already updated.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The remaining warning is a small, concrete workflow change suitable for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items
- [ ] Add `permissions: {}` to the `preflight` job in `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml`.
